## Launch counting and the S4 table {#sec-ch16-launches}

### Summary

The eager step of V3 is launch-bound: its cost on a GPU[^rg-d1be4fb0f62d] follows the number of kernels, copies and fills it asks
the device to run, more than the arithmetic inside them. @sec-ch11 compares that cost with the pre-V3 code and
with the graph path, and it needs a count that two people can take the same way. This section gives that
procedure: profile a few steps after a timed run, export the profiler's trace, and count the device events of
three kinds per step. The S4 table that applies the procedure, and the bound ruled from it, are committed in the
S4 record on the closing-plan branch; this chapter cites them and repeats none of their numbers.[^ch16-s4-src]

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Count the device launches of one step, the same way on every build and every cell of the S4 table.

**Data.** Reads one run of a deck; writes the run's JSON report, `OUT.prof.txt` (the profiler tables) and, with
`SPEED_PROF_TRACE` set, `OUT.trace.json` (the profiler's chrome trace).

**Placement.** Outside the solver: `bench.py` drives the block or Mesh, times its steps, then profiles a few more.

**Activation.** `bench.py --deck <deck> --device cuda --profile <n>` with `SPEED_PROF_TRACE=1`. Default: not run.

**Guarantee / limits.** A count, not a time: exact for the trace it is taken from, with no tolerance; it can
differ by a few events between a host and driver pair and another (the S4 record notes such an offset).

**Evidence.** No ctest at the pin (@tbl-ch16-launches-tests); the record is the S4 file.
:::

Local symbols of this section: $n_{\mathrm{prof}}$ the number of profiled steps; $N_{\mathrm{ev}}$ the events counted in
the trace; $L_{\mathrm{step}}$ the launches per step.

### Derivation

None: the count is a definition. Over $n_{\mathrm{prof}}$ profiled steps,

$$
L_{\mathrm{step}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{ev}}}{n_{\mathrm{prof}}}, \qquad
N_{\mathrm{ev}} = \#\{\text{trace events of category } \texttt{kernel}, \texttt{gpu\_memcpy} \text{ or } \texttt{gpu\_memset}\}.
$$ {#eq-ch16-launches}

@eq-ch16-launches counts what the device ran, not what the host issued. On the graph path the kernels replayed
inside a graph appear in the trace one by one, so $L_{\mathrm{step}}$ on that path is the work of a step, comparable with the
eager count; the number of calls the host makes per step is much smaller, and is a different quantity that the
S4 record reports separately.

### Numerical method

**One count.** `bench.py` builds the deck's block (or Mesh), runs `--warmup` steps, times `--steps` steps, and
then, with `--profile n`, runs $n_{\mathrm{prof}} = n$ more steps inside `torch.profiler` with CPU and CUDA activities,
synchronising before and after. With `SPEED_PROF_TRACE` set it exports the chrome trace; in every case it writes
the profiler's tables sorted by device time and by host time. The count of @eq-ch16-launches is taken from the
trace by event category; at the cited commit no script that does that count is committed with the tool, so the
count is a filter over the trace's `cat` field.

**Which path ran.** A count is only meaningful with the path that produced it. The run's JSON report carries
the block's `execution_report()` counters (captures, replays, eager segment runs;
{{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::report >}}) and its capability, whose `eager_reasons` say why
any segment ran eager ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::capability >}}). A graph-path count
with eager runs in its report is a mixed count and is labelled so.

**The S4 cells.** The S4 record applies this to four cells: the Straka case with HLLC in float64, the shipped
Straka deck, a six-panel moist cubed sphere, and the same with the implicit solve and a varying step. Each cell
is counted with the pre-V3 build and the V3 build, eager and default; the record states the device each column
was counted on.

### Code

**How to use it.**

```sh
SPEED_PROF_TRACE=1 python bench.py --deck cubed6_moist.yaml --device cuda \
    --warmup 5 --steps 100 --threads 8 --profile 4 --out c3_default.json
# then count the kernel, gpu_memcpy and gpu_memset events of c3_default.json.trace.json and divide by 4
```

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing: the procedure reads a trace. A deck the executor cannot capture still
gives a count, of the eager path, and its report says so.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the path a counted step took | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::report >}} | `StageExecutor::report` | `execution` |
| why a segment ran eager | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::capability >}} | `StageExecutor::capability` | none |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The count depends on the host, driver and device: the S4 record notes the same build counting a few events
  apart on two cards, so two counts are compared only when taken on one machine.
- The trace counts events, not their cost: two steps with the same count can take different times.
- No script for the count itself is committed; the filter over the trace is part of the procedure as written,
  not of a tool.
- The S4 numbers belong to the commits the record names; they are cited, not re-measured, at this chapter's pin.
:::
